books.name: Flagship

thesis_full.summary: IWM is the mechanical leadership sleeve holding — the 96.8th percentile sector ETF by 252-day relative-strength, trend-confirmed above its 200-day moving average. Size is equal-weight within the leadership budget (0%).
thesis_full.why_now: IWM ranks in the 96.8th percentile for 12-month RS and clears the 200-day trend gate, making it the doctrine's 'present in the leader mechanically' expression — holding the sector without chasing the single name underneath.
bear: Leadership rotation: held ONLY while RS stays top-decile (currently 96.8th percentile) — exits mechanically if RS drops below the 70th percentile; no discretion.
Breadth / narrowing risk: sector ETF performance can be driven by a handful of mega-cap names; if underlying breadth narrows the ETF masks single-name concentration risk.
Extension vs 200-day MA unknown (no stockdata for this ETF) — assume normal mean-reversion risk applies; monitor pct_vs_200dma.
Mechanical sleeve: no single-name conviction here; macro de-risk (regime quad flip or liquidity-overlay) trims the leadership budget first — exits are systematic, not qualitative.
thesis_full.what_would_prove_wrong: IWM breaks below its 200-day moving average for 3+ consecutive sessions, or drops below the 70th RS percentile relative to the sector universe.
thesis_full.sizing_rationale: Leadership sleeve: equal-weighted across the trend-gated top RS sectors. Weight = 0% (sleeve budget ÷ number of qualifying leaders). No confluence gate required; the trend filter is the only gate.

Frame: Q3 Stagflation (confidence 0.185, pending Q2), liquidity neutral with an easing impulse, Fear/Euphoria in Greed but 'divergent, no consensus' (breadth/margin risk-off vs turnover/copper-gold risk-on). By doctrine I detect what has already turned rather than chase the desk's mean-reversion-into-laggards idea, since Defense/NEV/Coal show no price follow-through. The desk instead keeps corroborating my own names with 'now/imminent' urgency and intact entries, so I add conviction there. Anchor 振德医疗 (603301.SS, 15%, alpha leader intact); CXO uptrend 药石科技 (300725.SZ, 12%); winner-let-run 京新药业 (002020.SZ, 11%, +15%); highest-conviction bottoming add 一品红 (300723.SZ, 10%, conviction 71 HIGH); gaming diversifier 三七互娱 (002555.SZ, 10%, α 0.82); early-base starter 海正药业 (600267.SS, 8%). All six confirmed priceable in native CNY.
decisions.thesis: No exits. Rebalance is additive within the existing thesis: added conviction to 一品红 (300723.SZ, ~5.3%→10%), 三七互娱 (002555.SZ, ~8%→10%) and 海正药业 (600267.SS, ~6%→8%), funded from cash; anchor/winner/uptrend names held near current weights. Passed on the desk's laggard mean-reversion ideas (Defense/NEV/Coal) and off-thesis buy-zone names (e.g. 鸣志电器) for lack of confirmed price follow-through / negative alpha."

positions.name: Tencent

decisions.subject: China book
decisions.lean: HK book benchmarked to FXI, repositioned from a 58%-cash posture (an unconfirmed short-vs-benchmark bet) to ~34% cash with a defensive tilt. The China read is genuinely low-confidence: Q3 stagflation but pending-Q2 recovery, easing impulse building, Fear/Euphoria in Greed (72, divergent). HK is growth-scare/risk-off with a weak peg, yet the desk flags HK Financials/Banks leading relative strength and property recovering. Desk buy boards are thin (only Power Assets on the HK board; intake empty), so I keep a meaningful cash buffer rather than chasing unconfirmed names. Structure: Tencent (0700.HK) + a modest Alibaba (9988.HK) as the tech/offense anchor and to cap my single biggest FXI tracking gap; China Life (2628.HK) + ICBC (1398.HK) + Bank of China (3988.HK) as the financials/dividend-defense sleeve that the HK RS read supports; China Mobile (0941.HK) as a new defensive telecom FXI anchor; CSPC Pharmaceutical (1093.HK) riding the innovative-drugs momentum; Power Assets (0006.HK) as utility defense and the one name the HK buy board still flags. Offense ~22%, defense ~40%, ~34% cash — consistent with the shadow ROTATE_DEFENSIVE posture and low conviction.
decisions.thesis: No outright exits. Reduced cash from ~58% to ~34% by adding two new defensive/tracking anchors — China Mobile (0941.HK) and a modest Alibaba (9988.HK) — and modestly sizing up the existing financials and Tencent. Kept both H-share banks (ICBC, Bank of China) despite being underwater because the HK-specific RS read favors HK financials and they pay defensive dividends.
